pairs.why: A's large translucent bell and long, flowing ribbon arms fill the frame and match the real jellyfish's soft, airy build; B's arms are a short, compact ruffled clump.
B is a plain dark-blue cylinder like the real light, while A's added barn-door flaps make it a different kind of fixture.
A's bright yellow bumpers and trim make it look like a plastic toy; B keeps the real card's calm dark-blue metal finish.
The two are nearly the same, but A's lamp is bigger and more solid and fills the frame more, closer to the real card's bold main shape.
B's smoother, simpler map sheets with flat colour sit closer to the real card's clean finish than A's crumpled paper with drawn mountains.
B has the real card's thick white borders and bold, solid stacked sheets, though it is glossier than the real card; A reads as worn, crumpled parchment.
B's flatter sheets with pale borders and cleaner green fill sit nearer the real stack than A's beige, crumpled paper with heavier texture.
A's soft, pillowy panels and bold canopy that fills the frame match the real umbrella's puffy finish; B's canopy is flatter, thinner and smaller.
